title: Model-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Enabling Precision Dosing Via Adaptive Dosing

content.abstract_summary: Tutorial review of reinforcement learning (RL) coupled with population PK/PD models for precision dosing. Covers: RL framework components (state, action, reward) for dosing problems; case studies including propofol-induced anesthesia, warfarin anticoagulation, and anticancer treatments; how PK/PD models serve as the simulation engine for RL training. Identifies heterogeneity in approaches and proposes a standard problem formulation. From the U Pavia group (Tosca, De Carlo, Magni) — the leading academic group developing model-informed RL for precision dosing. Published in Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics.
key_findings: RL naturally fits the sequential decision-making paradigm of adaptive dosing: clinicians adapt doses based on patient response and evolution monitoring, exactly the structure RL is designed for

PK/PD models as simulation engines for RL training enable safe, data-rich training environments: virtual patient populations can be simulated without patient risk, enabling RL to explore suboptimal or dangerous dosing that could never be ethically tested clinically

Case studies cover: (1) propofol anesthesia — one of the earliest and most developed RL dosing applications; (2) warfarin anticoagulation — narrow therapeutic window, INR feedback; (3) anticancer treatments — most diverse, covering agents with different PD biomarkers
Identified heterogeneity in: precision dosing approaches, RL methodologies used, and degree of adherence to clinical domain — the field lacks standardization comparable to population PK modeling

Tutorial on problem formulation: state space (patient biomarkers, PK parameters, drug concentrations), action space (dose amounts and intervals), reward function design (target concentration ranges, safety penalties)
Integration of PK/PD models into RL holds great promise but further investigation is needed — identifies the translational gap between simulation results and clinical deployment
limitations: Current heterogeneity in RL dosing methodology and clinical adherence means results across studies are not directly comparable — an identified gap the review calls for the field to address

Further investigations needed to address current limitations and extend applicability to drugs requiring adaptive dosing — the review acknowledges the field is still pre-clinical for most applications
No new primary results — this is a review and tutorial, not a methods paper with novel experiments

extracted_claims.text: Reinforcement learning naturally fits this paradigm: it perfectly mimics the sequential decision-making process where clinicians adapt dose administration based on patient response and evolution monitoring.
The integration of PK/PD models into a RL-framework holds great promise for precision dosing, but further investigations and advancements are still needed to address current limitations.

gaps_addressed: The definitive tutorial/review for M3 (RL for precision dosing) from the leading group in this area — a WG scoping paper or tutorial on RL+pharmacometrics should cite this as the primary review of the field
The standard problem formulation (state/action/reward structure for dosing) is directly usable as a template for the WG's RL tutorial component of the scoping paper

The heterogeneity finding creates a clear gap for the WG to address: proposing standardized RL+PKPD benchmarking is a concrete contribution analogous to karlsen_2025's call for standardized covariate selection benchmarks

provenance.notes: Found via PubMed search 'reinforcement learning drug dosing pharmacokinetics optimal' (PMID 38989560). CPT 2024, 116(3):619-636. University of Pavia (Tosca EM, De Carlo A, Ronchi D, Magni P). This is the review companion to de_carlo_2024 and de_carlo_2025 from the same group. No PMC entry found — not open access.
